title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GRUMPY GIL
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gil Brennan, a snowplow driver in Buffalo, New York.
Gil could clear ten miles of snow before sunrise, but not one breakfast without a complaint.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PICKLE JAR
segments.quote: Content makes poor men rich; discontent makes rich men poor.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: The coffee was weak. The Bills were hopeless.
His wife, Patty, put a pickle jar on the counter. One dollar per complaint.
By Friday it held forty-one dollars, and a line from Ben Franklin on the lid:
Content makes poor men rich; discontent makes rich men poor.
Gil could not afford to be grumpy. He promised thirty days, no complaints.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BIG STORM
segments.quote: How much pain have cost us the evils which have never happened!
segments.author: Thomas Jefferson
lines: Then the forecast said three feet of snow.
Gil lay awake, sure the truck would break.
At three a.m., he read his old boss's note in the garage, from Thomas Jefferson:
How much pain have cost us the evils which have never happened!
So he stopped worrying and drove out. The old truck ran like a dream.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE SAME OLD ROUTE
segments.quote: Things do not change; we change.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: Gil had plowed the same route for twenty-two years. Same streets. Same potholes.
Patty left a library book on his dashboard, by Henry David Thoreau:
Things do not change; we change.
So Gil started looking. A baker waved at four a.m.
Gil waved back. Same route. Better view.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE DRIVEWAY
segments.quote: Always do right. This will gratify some people and astonish the rest.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: One morning his plow buried Mrs. Ferraro's driveway. She was eighty-four.
Gil could have kept driving. Then he thought of Mark Twain:
Always do right. This will gratify some people and astonish the rest.
So he dug her out by hand. Mrs. Ferraro was gratified. Patty was astonished.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THANKSGIVING
segments.quote: Reflect upon your present blessings, of which every man has many, not on your past misfortunes, of which all men have some.
segments.author: Charles Dickens
lines: At Thanksgiving, his brother Mike listed everything that went wrong this year.
Gil had a list. A bad knee. A leaky roof.
Then Patty raised her glass with a line from Charles Dickens:
Reflect upon your present blessings, of which every man has many, not on your past misfortunes, of which all men have some.
Gil folded his list and thanked everyone by name. Mike cried into the mashed potatoes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PORCH
segments.quote: To be happy at home is the ultimate result of all ambition.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: By spring, the jar had hardly grown. One dollar went in when the Bills lost.
They spent it all on two rocking chairs.
There, Patty read him a line from the English writer Samuel Johnson:
To be happy at home is the ultimate result of all ambition.
Gil looked at the melting snow, at Patty, at his weak coffee. He called it perfect.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Be content. Don't borrow worry. Change your view. Do right. Count your blessings. Be happy at home.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Be content. Don't borrow worry. Change your view. Do right. Count your blessings. Be happy at home.
Me? I only complain about my barber. He charges me full price.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
